extracted.intended_audience: Users and authors of the Singular computer algebra system (computational algebraists / symbolic computation researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for Singular library procedures (grobcov.lib, inout.lib, modular.lib, parallel.lib, etc.), giving expected inputs, calling sequences, outputs, options, and notes/examples for each routine. Intended as a programming / usage guideline for computing loci, envelopes, modular computations and for I/O and parallel helpers.

rubrics_metrics.name: locusdg
rubrics_metrics.description: locusdg(list L) — Procedure from grobcov.lib. The output is the list of the "Relevant" components of the locus in Dynamic Geometry [C1,..,C:m], where Ci = [pi,[pi1,..], "Relevant", level_i].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: locusdg(locus(S)). The "Relevant" components are the components classified as "Normal" and "Accumulation" (see help for locus). Return: list of components with canonical P-representation and taxonomy label. Note: This routine expects the input to be the output of locus(...) and returns only components flagged as Relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: envelop
rubrics_metrics.description: envelop(poly F, ideal C[, options]) — compute the envelope of a family of hypersurfaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements: F must be the family polynomial F(x1..xn,u1..um). ideal C must be the ideal of restrictions on parameters u1..um and should contain fewer polynomials than the number of parameters (s < m). Calling sequence: ring R=(0,x1,..,xn),(u1,..,um),lp; poly F=F(...); ideal C=g1(..),..,gs(...); envelop(F,C[,options]). Output: list of components [C1,..,Cn] where each Ci = [pi,[pi1,..],tax]. Taxonomy info: for normal-point components tax=[d,taxonomy,anti-image] with d=dimension of anti-image, taxonomy="Normal" or "Special", anti-image=values of mover corresponding to the component. For non-normal-point components tax=[d,taxonomy] with taxonomy="Accumulation" or "Degenerate". Options: pairs of (string,int). Supported options include "comments", c (default 0; set to 1 for comments) and "anti-image", a (default a=1 to show anti-image for Normal components; set a=0 to hide). Notes: grobcov and locus are called internally. Base ring must be of form Q[x][u] (x = parameters, u = variables). Uses generalized definition of envelope from Montes' Groebner Cover. Examples provided (Steiner Deltoid).

rubrics_metrics.name: locusto
rubrics_metrics.description: locusto(list L) — transform the output of locus/locusdg/envelop into a string in standard form readable by other languages (e.g., GeoGebra).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: locusto(L) where L is the output of locus(...), locusdg(...), or envelop(...). Return: locus in string standard form. Note: Can only be called after computing locus/locusdg/envelop as described. Example outputs show canonical string representation with component taxonomy and anti-image information.

rubrics_metrics.name: stdlocus
rubrics_metrics.description: stdlocus(ideal F) — determine the irreducible components (tops) of a locus using standard Groebner basis elimination and prime decomposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements: Input ideal F must be the set of equations defining the locus. The input ring must be parametric (basering Q[x][u] where x = tracer variables/parameters and u = remaining variables). Calling sequence: stdlocus(S). Return: list of the tops (prime ideals) p_i of irreducible components. Notes: This routine uses only standard GB, elimination and prime decomposition rather than grobcov; it does not determine taxonomy (Normal/Special/Accumulation) nor the holes of components. Intended as a simpler alternative when taxonomy is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: AssocTanToEnv
rubrics_metrics.description: AssocTanToEnv(poly F, ideal C, ideal E[, options]) — given a family F and a computed envelope component E, returns parameter values of the associated tangent hypersurface(s) at points of E.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements: ring R = Q[x1..xn][u1..um]. F = F(x,u) family polynomial, C = ideal of restrictions in variables u, E must be a component of envelop(F,C) previously computed. Calling sequence as above. Return: list [lpp,basis,segment]; basis determines the associated tangent hyper-surface at a point of E; the segment is given in Prep. Notes: grobcov called internally. Example: demonstrates computing basis for associated tangent (and substituting parameter values to get tangent equation). Useful to obtain parameter values (e.g., t=(5/12)*y0) that define associated tangent.

rubrics_metrics.name: FamElemsAtEnvCompPoints
rubrics_metrics.description: FamElemsAtEnvCompPoints(poly F, ideal C, ideal E[, options]) — returns parameter values of all family elements that pass through a point of an envelope component E.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements: F in R=Q[x1..xn][u1..um], C ideal of restrictions on u1..um (s < m), E is a component of envelop(F,C) previously computed. Calling sequence: FamElemsAtEnvCompPoints(F,C,E[,options]). Return: list [lpp,basis,segment]. The basis determines parameter values of hypersurfaces passing through a fixed point of E; lpp gives the dimension of the set; segment is the component in Prep. Fixing x-values inside E, the basis allows determining values of parameters (u1..um) of hypersurfaces through that point. Note: grobcov called internally; basering must be Q[a][x] (a = parameters, x = variables). Example shows unique associated tangent family for given point.

rubrics_metrics.name: discrim
rubrics_metrics.description: discrim(f,x) — compute the factorized discriminant of polynomial f with respect to variable x (for sign discussion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements: f must be a polynomial in Q[a][x] or Q[x] of degree 2 in x. x can be a variable or a parameter of the ring. Usage: discrim(f,x). Return: factorized discriminant of f wrt x (useful to discuss sign changes). Example shown with f=a*x^2*y + b*x*y + c*y leading to factors like y and (4*a*c-b^2).

rubrics_metrics.name: WLemma
rubrics_metrics.description: WLemma(F,A[,options]) — compute reduced Groebner basis of specialization of F over a segment S determined by Wibmer's Lemma.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments: F ideal in Q[a][x] (or Q[x][u] notation as parameters vs variables), A ideal in Q[a] (top of segment). Calling sequence: ring R=(0,x1..xn),(u1..um),lp; ideal F=..., ideal A=...; WLemma(F,A[,options]). Return: list [lpp,B,S] where B is the reduced Groebner basis of the specialized F over segment S (subset of V(A) with top A) given by I-regular functions; S is given in P- or C-representation. Options: ("rep",0) default P-representation, ("rep",1) C-representation. Notes: basering must be Q[a][x] (a = parameters, x = variables). Reference: Montes & Wibmer. Examples in manual illustrate returned bases and segments.

rubrics_metrics.name: intersectpar
rubrics_metrics.description: intersectpar(list S) — compute the intersection of a list of ideals I1,...,Ik in Q[x,a].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: interectpar(list of ideals S) (note name appears as interectpar in text / header 'intersectpar'). The routine is called in ring Q[a][x]. The ideals I1..Ik can depend only on [a] or on [x,a]. Return: the intersection ideal in Q[x,a]. Examples illustrate combining ideals depending on parameters and variables. Useful when you need the common constraints across parameterized ideals.

rubrics_metrics.name: ADGT
rubrics_metrics.description: ADGT(ideal H, ideal T, ideal H1, ideal T1[, options]) — analyze a geometric proposition (H and not H1) => (T and not T1) and compute supplementary parameter conditions that make the proposition a theorem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments: H (hypothesis) ideal in Q[a][x]; T (thesis) ideal in Q[a][x]; H1 negative hypothesis ideal (depending only on parameters a); T1 negative thesis ideal in Q[a][x]. Calling sequence: ADGT(H,T,H1,T1[,options]). Return: list [[1,S1],[2,S2],..] where S1,S2 are parameter sets (given in Prep) that must hold as supplementary conditions for the proposition to become a theorem. If the proposition is generally true, ADGT also returns the "generic segment" (unless option disables it) giving information about determined variable values for every parameter value. Options: ("rep",0) default P-representation, ("rep",1) C-representation; ("gseg",0/1) default "gseg",1 which includes generic segment; set "gseg",0 to avoid. Requirement: basering R must be Q[a][x]; ideals defined on R. Examples include triangle/isogonal computations and an automatic demonstration of the Nine Points Circle Theorem (shows how to read generic segment and returned constraints).

rubrics_metrics.name: allprint
rubrics_metrics.description: allprint(L) — print list L[1], L[2], ... if integer ALLprint exists, and optionally pause for interactive inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: allprint(L); L is a list. Behavior: prints elements of L and makes a pause if global integer ALLprint > 0. Note: ALLprint must be declared/exported; example shows printing matrices and using kill ALLprint to remove the global. Return: none. Intended for interactive debugging/printing of long lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: lprint
rubrics_metrics.description: lprint(id[,n]) — produce a string representation of id (poly/ideal/vector/module/matrix) formatted into lines of length n without breaking monomials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: lprint(id[,n]); default n = pagewidth. id is printed columnwise; lprint(transpose(id)) can be used to format matrices as input strings. Each column separated by a blank line. Return: string (if assigned) in format suitable for input. Use with execute(...) to reconstruct matrices/ideals. Examples show formatting of polynomials and modules and re-executing the string to verify equality. Useful for generating input-friendly textual representations and for copy/paste between systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: pmat
rubrics_metrics.description: pmat(M[,n]) — produce a string representing matrix M in array format fitting into pagewidth (or truncate columns to n characters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: pmat(M[,n]); M is a matrix, n integer optional. Return: string representing M in array format; if each column fits pagewidth, full representation returned; if n is given (>1) only the first n characters of each column shown and truncated columns indicated by '..'. Useful for compact printing of matrices or truncated previews. Examples illustrate normal and truncated outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: rMacaulay
rubrics_metrics.description: rMacaulay(s[,n]) — convert a string producing Macaulay Classic output into a string readable by Singular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: rMacaulay(s[,n]); s is a string (contents from Macaulay Classic). If n provided, first n lines of file are deleted (useful when Macaulay putstd added headers). Return: a string that can be used in Singular as input (e.g., to create an ideal or matrix). Note: backslash and escaping differences can hinder direct cut-and-paste; examples show converting polynomial and matrix representations and then executing the generated string via execute(...) to create ideal/matrix objects in Singular.

rubrics_metrics.name: show
rubrics_metrics.description: show(id) or show(R,s) — compact display of an object with metadata (type, generator counts, minimal polynomial for qring, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: show(id); id any object of base ring or a ring/qring. show(R,s) where R is a ring and s is string (name of object in R) displays object belonging to R. Behavior: prints compact format with some information: object type, number of generators for ideals/modules, ring minpoly, quotient ideal for qring, etc. Return: none. Note: show(R,s) does not work inside a procedure; lists passed to show must not contain a ring. Examples demonstrate show on rings, ideals, vectors, modules, maps and quotient rings.

rubrics_metrics.name: showrecursive
rubrics_metrics.description: showrecursive(id,p[,ord]) — display id in recursive polynomial format treating p as polynomial variables to expand recursively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: showrecursive(id,p[,ord]); ord is ordering string (default "dp"). Behavior: displays id as polynomial in variables occurring in p with coefficients in remaining variables by mapping to a ring with parameters and applying show. Return: none. Example: showrecursive(f,x) prints polynomial in x with coefficient expressions; showrecursive(f,xy,"lp") shows expansion in lex order. Useful for readable nested polynomial displays.

rubrics_metrics.name: split
rubrics_metrics.description: split(s[,n]) — split string s into lines of length n separated by '\'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: split(s[,n]); default n = pagewidth. Return: same string split into lines separated by backslash and newline. Commonly used together with lprint to format long polynomial strings cleanly for display or further processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: tab
rubrics_metrics.description: tab(n) — return a string of n space tabs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: tab(n); Return: string with n spaces (tabs). Example shows using tab to build simple formatted ASCII patterns. Useful for aligning printed output programmatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: pause
rubrics_metrics.description: pause([prompt]) — interrupt execution and wait for user input; display prompt if provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: pause([prompt]); prompt is optional string (default displays 'pause' or custom message). Return: none. Purpose: interrupt execution, useful in procedures combined with printlevel to stop and display intermediate results until user presses return. Note: only works interactively. Example shows how to use pause("press <return> to continue").

rubrics_metrics.name: modular
rubrics_metrics.description: modular(command, arguments[, primeTest, deleteUnluckyPrimes, pTest, finalTest, pmax]) — run a command using modular (mod p) techniques and lift results to characteristic 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: modular(command, arguments[, primeTest, deleteUnluckyPrimes, pTest, finalTest, pmax]). command is a string naming a Singular command (e.g., "std"), arguments is a list of arguments for that command. Optional procedures primeTest/deleteUnluckyPrimes/pTest/finalTest control correctness checks; pmax is an upper bound for primes (default is largest int-prime or 2^29-based prime for parameter rings). Return: result of command applied to arguments computed using modular methods. Requirements: the type of result must be bigint, ideal, module, or matrix. Notes: modular techniques run computations modulo several primes and reconstruct via Chinese remaindering and Farey rational map to avoid coefficient swell and to parallelize computations. Default behavior assumes tests succeed and primes are lucky. See references and modstd.lib for algorithmic details. Example demonstrates modular("std", list(I)).

rubrics_metrics.name: parallelWaitN
rubrics_metrics.description: parallelWaitN(commands, arguments, N[, timeout]) — run multiple commands in parallel and wait for N tasks to finish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: commands is a list of command strings, arguments is a list of argument-lists, N is an int number of tasks to wait for, timeout optional in ms (default 0 disables timeout). Return: list containing results of commands[i] applied to arguments[i] for the tasks that finished; size of returned list equals number of finished tasks (>=N if multiple finish concurrently). Behavior: waits until N jobs finish or timeout/error. Entries for tasks that did not finish (timeout or error) are the string "none". The returned list may contain more than N results if several finishes coincide, or fewer than N in case of timeout/errors. Notes: entries of commands must be strings and corresponding arguments must be lists. Useful to coordinate parallel job pools; examples show computing std() on distinct ideals in parallel.

rubrics_metrics.name: parallelWaitFirst
rubrics_metrics.description: parallelWaitFirst(commands, arguments[, timeout]) — wait for the first completed task among a list (synonym for parallelWaitN(...,1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: parallelWaitFirst(commands, arguments[, timeout]) is equivalent to parallelWaitN(commands, arguments, 1[, timeout]). Return: list containing at least one result (unless timeout). Behavior and argument constraints identical to parallelWaitN. Useful to retrieve the earliest available result among several parallel computations.
